liam_w: Heads-up — after flipping to the new FlashV3 variant for long-context production requests we see a tokens/sec regression and unit-cost increase. Anyone else seeing this?
monica_g: Oof, can you paste the before/after numbers + runtime flags you changed?
liam_w: baseline (paged-attn tuned): 12.4k tok/s, ~$1.85 per M tokens. flash-v3 rollout: 10.1k tok/s, ~$2.27 per M. ~18% drop in throughput, ~22% $/M increase. KV cache hit rate ~73%. batch dist: 60% tiny (<8), 30% mid (8-128), 10% long (>512).
javier_r: that batch mix is rough for flashv3 — it shines on long steady sequences. small-batch overhead + kernel launch costs can swamp wins. did kernel selection fall back to a less optimal path for small sequences?
liam_w: profiler top lines (sample):
```
attn_kernel_select: flashv3_variant_main 48%
flashv3_small_seq_path 31%
paged_attn_fallback 12%
kernel_launch_overhead 9%
```
looks like the runtime is still trying small-seq flash kernels a lot.
javier_r: hmmm. two angles: 1) batching heuristic is grouping too many tiny sequences into flash small-path which has higher per-batch latency for tiny token counts; 2) KV cache behavior — 73% hit rate isn't terrible, but if prefetching triggers more work on flash it could inflate cost.
karen_s: can you dump a sample request trace with batch sizes and seq lengths? the scheduler metrics would help: `batch.mean_size`, `batch.small_frac`, `fallback_rate` over the window.
liam_w: pasted sample trace excerpt:
```
window: 60s
batches: 1200
batch.mean_size: 4.2
batch.small_frac: 0.62
fallback_rate: 0.18
seq_len_p95: 820
kv_prefetches/sec: 42
```
bench-bot: starting A/B run: job 5532 comparing paged-attn tuned vs flashv3 with adjusted heuristics (runs: 20 each). ETA ~45m.
monica_g: suggested quick mitigations: 1) force paged fallback for batches with mean_size < 6, 2) enable `heuristics.small_batch_accel=false` for flashv3 until we tune the microkernel, 3) reduce kv_prefetch concurrency to see if IO/spike amplification is an issue.
javier_r: long-term: we should add a cost-model into the kernel selector that estimates $/M tokens given batch mix and KV hit rate. quick patch to selector: if estimated tokens/sec_gain < 5% and small_frac>0.5 -> prefer paged.
liam_w: creating a quick repro script and an ops PR to toggle selector. repro script: `scripts/repro_longbatch.sh --mix 60,30,10 --kvhit 0.73 --variant flashv3` — will share results.
devops-bot: perf-test cluster pool autoscaled to +2 GPUs for bench job 5532.
liam_w: initial A/B halfway: paged-attn median 12.3k tok/s, flashv3 median 10.2k tok/s. small-batch forced paged patch applied on a canary node and tok/s jumped to 12.1k (close to baseline).
karen_s: ok that's enough signal. plan: revert flashv3 auto-selection for mixed-small workloads, open tracking ticket INF-3421 to instrument selector cost model + add a rollout gate.
monica_g: also add a perf regression alert in console for $/M change >10% for a model route. prevents noisy rollouts. :+1:
liam_w: filing INF-3421 now, attaching traces and bench outputs. thanks all.
